papers.title: Physics and astrophysics research: source-based research tasks
H0LiCOW XIII. A 2.4% measurement of H0 from lensed quasars: 5.3σ tension between early and late-Universe probes
papers.task_relation: The local TDLMC task infers a distance posterior from simulated imaging, delays, PSFs, and kinematics. It isolates a lens-inference subproblem; its likelihood assumptions and posterior score do not reproduce the six-quasar observational analysis or its cosmological conclusions.
papers.primary_goal: Measure the Hubble constant and constrain cosmology using time-delay distances from gravitationally lensed quasars.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Infer time-delay distances from strongly lensed quasars to constrain the cosmic expansion rate.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Lensing distances and the resulting cosmological constraints are the primary scientific measurements in H0LiCOW XIII.
science_relevance.reason: The evidence directly studies the physical quantity estimated by the task; a time-delay challenge announcement alone is insufficient.
science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
